newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Kia union to let company set wage hike.
newsitem.headline: Kia union to let company set wage hike.

text.p: The union at South Korean carmaker Kia Motors Corp said on Thursday it would allow management to determine this year's wage increase in an effort to cooperate in overcoming the company's hardships.
"The union and management have agreed to jointly respond to the current crisis in light of the continuing domestic economic slump," a union statement said.
The union's decision was widely seen as giving critical support to the carmaker, which has had difficulty securing a smooth flow of funds from local lenders.
Kia Motors' parent Kia Group has been fighting rumours and a growing reluctance among lenders to extend credits.
The company, one South Korea's top three carmakers, had in the past suffered from violent labour disputes.
Kia Group officials were due to meet with merchant bankers on Thursday to persuade them to open credit lines.
Nervous merchant banks, which have been portrayed as culprits in a series of post-Hanbo corporate failures, were blamed for calling in loans recently from the Kia Group.
Hanbo Steel went insolvent in January under some $5.8 billion in debt, causing financial institutions to tighten credit lines.
Kia Group chairman Kim Sun-hong had asked finance minister Kang Kyong-shik to persuade merchant banks to keep cash flowing to the conglomerate. -- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727-5646
